title: Trenier's father, Willie Bolero and Thomas Daley
summary: Pope names the father of the Trenier brothers and alto player Willie Bolero, called Chicken; the interviewer mentions Thomas Daley.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Yes. Yes. You mentioned the Trenier brothers, I think it was. Trenier, yes.

Trenier. Now, he's the father of the Trenier brothers. They're very famous right now. Because they just left Vegas, I think, back home. They moved from Mobile to Los Angeles. And he's one that still lives. I have another one that lives now. It's called Willie Bolero. What was that name?

Bolero, like a Spanish name. Bolero, yes. And, of course, he was one of the late members, you know. He just trained him myself. He'd come along and go every day, you know. But my father practically gives it up.

There was one musician I was going to ask about. I met a male man downtown this morning who is a musician too. And he told me there was a fellow, he didn't know his real name, they just call him Chicken. And he's a jazz at the cathedral.
Well, that's Bolero. That's Bolero. Oh, that's... That's Bolero. That's right. And he's still in town.
He's still in town, yes. And he used to play with the Excelsior band.

He used to play with the Excelsior band, the original band. What did he play? He played alto. Alto? Alto, hi. He's the man. You know, he played, you know, ta, Yes, I know that. You know what I'm talking about.

Yes, indeed. This male man I met, his name is Thomas Daley. Thomas Daley? Thomas Daley Senior. And he knows this man. He knows you, too. You mentioned this other man was about your age, he thought, or maybe even older.

That's right. He may be a year older than I have. That's Bolero, we have reference. Yes. So we'll get to see. Well, Daley, back in the middle, I think you might have met some of the younger... Probably.
He was a younger man. He was a male man.
I don't think he played with the Excelsior band.
